cohort: 685,137 low-risk pregnant women with a history of cesarean delivery from the Nationwide Inpatient Sample (2003-2011)
finding: Low-risk women who attempted a TOL after cesarean were at an increased risk of overall morbidity (OR 1.74) and specifically uterine rupture (OR 22.52) compared to those who opted for a repeat cesarean.
mod_finding: Low-risk women undergoing a trial of labor after cesarean remain at increased risk of adverse maternal events as compared with those who chose elective repeat cesarean delivery.
